text:
Tariq (Support): FYI customer C-9873 reporting large latency spikes from EU users since ~09:10 UTC. They see 600-1200ms for simple text.generate calls (normally ~30-60ms). attaching trace id: `01-4b7f9a-9c3e5a`
Maya (SRE): can you paste the full trace link + the sample request (curl) they used? also what region are they in and which model/route? :eyes:
Tariq (Support): trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/01-4b7f9a-9c3e5a  model=redwood/gpt-neo-2.7b route=default acct=acct-803 EU client IP ~ 52.31.x.x
Tariq (Support): sample curl they used: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-neo-2.7b","input":"hi"}' -i`
Jin (Eng-Infra): looking at the trace quick snippet — I see the request hit our edge in eu-west-1 then forwarded to us-west-2 for inference, then response proxied back. that explains the RTT. Not expected for this account.
tracing-bot: sampled spans: edge-eu-west-1 -> router-eu-west-1 -> infer-us-west-2 -> cache-us-west-2 -> router-eu-west-1 -> edge-eu-west-1
Evan (Platform): that pattern can happen when the model shard or reserved capacity isn't available in primary region and router falls back to a compatible variant in another region. but we should never proxy back across regions — we should route the client directly to the serving region. sounds like a routing-proxy bug.
Maya (SRE): Jin, can you grep the router logs for `acct-803` and that trace id? I want to see the routing decision payload (`route_decision` field).
Jin (Eng-Infra): grabbing logs... snippet: `route_decision: {primary: eu-west-1, selected: us-west-2, reason: "capacity_unavailable", policy: "fallthrough-proxy"}` — aha the router used `fallthrough-proxy` instead of `redirect`. that will proxy via eu-west rather than telling client to connect to us-west.
Tariq (Support): is there a temporary customer-side workaround? can they force eu-only?
Evan (Platform): yes two options: 1) set header `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1` to pin region (server will reject if unavailable) or 2) set `region_preference` in account settings to `eu-west-1` (we can patch for them).
Maya (SRE): Jin — can you confirm if this `fallthrough-proxy` behavior was introduced with the last router change? I remember a config flip in canary yesterday.
Jin (Eng-Infra): confirmed. change 2026-02-18T03:12:22UTC changed default from `redirect` -> `fallthrough-proxy` for groups with `auto_fallback = true`. that was to avoid TLS/client-cert issues but it regresses latency for cross-region fallbacks.
Evan (Platform): plan: rollback the policy change on canary, hotfix router to prefer `redirect` when client region != selected region, and add metric alert on proxy-cross-region rate. Jin can you open a PR and a rollback + postmortem ticket?
Jin (Eng-Infra): creating PR now, will push canary rollback and include unit test for route header behavior.
Maya (SRE): in the meantime, Tariq, can you send the customer this temporary curl to pin EU and collect a new trace?
Maya (SRE): ```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-..." \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-neo-2.7b","input":"latency test"}'
```
Tariq (Support): sent to customer. they replied: when I add the header I get 68ms and `x-served-region: eu-west-1`. without header I get 980ms and `x-served-region: us-west-2`.
Evan (Platform): ok that's reproducible. Jin, after hotfix can we also add a short-lived route-affinity cache key clear for affected accounts so they stop hitting proxy?
Jin (Eng-Infra): will do. scheduling cache purge for acct-803 and any accounts that hit fallthrough in the last hour.
Tariq (Support): I told customer we found the cause and we have a rollback + patch in flight, gave them the header workaround. they appreciate the quick follow-up. :thumbsup:
Maya (SRE): filing incident summary and tagging oncall. we'll monitor for any other cross-region proxis. adding alert: `router.proxy_cross_region_rate > 0.5%` over 5m.
Evan (Platform): thanks team. follow-ups: PR #4827 (Jin), rollback on canary + promote after test, customer notif.
Tariq (Support): closing the support loop for now, will re-open if customer sees more spikes.
